javax.microedition.theme
Class ToolkitCapabilities

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.theme.ToolkitCapabilities

public class ToolkitCapabilities
extends java.lang.Object

Returns static information about the user interface toolkit related capabilities of the Mobile User Interface Customization API implementation found in the device.

Methods in this class typically take as parameters a feature and a role, as found in elements. The methods always deal with top-level elements, not members of element groups.

In methods that take a toolkitName parameter, the value must be one of the canonical user interface toolkit names as returned by the getSupportedToolkits() method.

Method Detail

getSupportedKinds

public static java.lang.String[] getSupportedKinds(java.lang.String feature,
                                                   java.lang.String role,
                                                   java.lang.String toolkitName)

Gets the supported content kinds of the toolkit element in some UI toolkit with the specified feature and role in this implementation. This method works like the getSupportedKinds method in the Capabilities class. The additional toolkitName parameter is the canonical toolkit name.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
toolkitName - the UI toolkit name
Returns:
an array of Element.KIND_XXX values, or a zero-length array if the element is not supported
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if any parameter is empty, or if toolkitName is not supported

getSupportedMediaTypes

public static java.lang.String[] getSupportedMediaTypes(java.lang.String feature,
                                                        java.lang.String role,
                                                        java.lang.String kind,
                                                        java.lang.String toolkitName)
                                                 throws ElementNotFoundException

Gets the supported media types for the toolkit element with the specified feature and role. This method works like the getSupportedMediaTypes method in the Capabilities class. The additional toolkitName parameter is the canonical toolkit name.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
kind - one of the Element.KIND_xxx constants
toolkitName - the UI toolkit name
Returns:
a string array of registered MIME type strings for the supplied kind, empty if registered MIME types do not apply to kind or the kind is not supported for the element
Throws:
ElementNotFoundException - if the base element with the specified feature and role is not supported by the implementation
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if any parameter is empty, or if kind is not one of those defined in the Element interface, or if toolkitName is not supported
See Also:
Capabilities.getSupportedMediaTypes(String, String, String)

getSupportedToolkits

public static java.lang.String[] getSupportedToolkits()

Gets the names of user interface toolkits supported by this implementation.

The returned array of String objects contains canonical names of the UI toolkits as specified in the "Toolkit names" section in the File Format Reference, one per supported toolkit. If the implementation does not support any UI toolkits, this method must return an empty array.

Returns:
array of canonical toolkit names, or empty if no toolkits supported

isElementCustomizable

public static boolean isElementCustomizable(java.lang.String feature,
                                            java.lang.String role,
                                            java.lang.String toolkitName)
                                     throws ElementNotFoundException

Determines if the toolkit element with the specified feature and role is customizable in the specified UI toolkit, according to the effective device customization policy.

If the isCustomizationPolicyEnabled method of the Capabilities class returns false, this method must return true.

If the customization of an element group is not customizable, all the child elements of the group must be implicitly not customizable.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
Returns:
true if toolkit element is customizable, false if not
Throws:
ElementNotFoundException - if the implementation does not support this feature and role combination for the specified toolkit
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if any parameter is empty, or if toolkitName is not a canonical name of a supported UI toolkit
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null

isToolkitElementSupported

public static boolean isToolkitElementSupported(java.lang.String feature,
                                                java.lang.String role,
                                                java.lang.String toolkitName)

Determines if the element with the specified feature and role is supported or not in a particular user interface toolkit. Supported customizable elements in UI toolkits are recommendations only, and depend on the actual toolkit implementations.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
toolkitName - name of user interface toolkit to query
Returns:
true if element is supported, false if not
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if any parameter is empty, or if toolkitName is not the canonical name of a supported UI toolkit
See Also:
getSupportedToolkits()
